title: Brew guides
content:
Brew guides

How to brew what we roast

Coffee is a ratio, a grind and a time. Get those three right and the rest is preference.

Filter

A pour-over, step by step

01

Weigh

Sixty grams of coffee to a litre of water. For one big cup: 18 g of coffee, 300 g of water.

02

Grind

Medium, like table salt. Grind it now, not this morning: coffee goes flat within the hour.

03

Bloom

Pour twice the coffee's weight in water, wait forty seconds, and watch it swell.

04

Pour

Add the rest in two goes, keeping the bed level. The whole brew should take about three minutes.

Cheat sheet

Ratios for everything else

Pour-over

60 g per litre, medium grind, 3 minutes

Cafetiere

60 g per litre, coarse grind, 4 minutes, then plunge

Espresso

18 g in, 36 g out, 28 seconds, fine grind

Moka pot

Fill the basket level, medium-fine, off the heat when it gurgles

Cold brew

80 g per litre, coarse, 16 hours in the fridge

Still not right?

Bitter usually means too fine or too long. Sour usually means too coarse or too quick. Change one thing at a time.

title: Our story
content:
Our story

A railway arch, a drum roaster and a lot of notebooks

We buy coffee we can trace, roast it in small batches and sell it while it is fresh. That is the whole business.

2019

It started because nobody would sell us a kilo

Two of us wanted good coffee at home and could only buy it by the cup. We bought a second-hand twelve-kilo roaster, put it in a railway arch, and spent a year making bad coffee until we stopped.

  • Twelve-kilo batches, roasted to order
  • Every bag carries its roast date, not a best-before
  • Compostable bags, posted first class
Shop this week's coffee

Four steps

How a coffee gets here

01

Buy

Through importers who publish what they paid the farm. If they will not say, we do not buy.

02

Sample

Every lot is roasted small and tasted on a table with eight cups before we commit.

03

Roast

Twelve kilos at a time, Tuesday, with the profile written down and kept.

04

Post

Bagged Wednesday morning and in the post by noon.

title: FAQ
content:
Help

Questions we are asked most

About the coffee, the subscriptions and how it reaches you.

Coffee

Everything is roasted on Tuesday and posted on Wednesday. The roast date is printed on the bag, not a best-before.

Whole bean if you own a grinder, because coffee goes flat within an hour of grinding. Otherwise pick the way you brew: filter for a dripper or cafetiere, espresso for a machine.

Sealed, about three months. Open, about two weeks before you notice. Keep it in the bag, folded shut, out of the fridge.

Orders and subscriptions

Change the coffee, the size, the grind or the date from your account, up to the Monday before a roast.

Yes, from your account, with no notice. Any coffee already roasted for you is sent.

Delivery

Orders placed before Monday evening are roasted Tuesday and posted Wednesday, first class. Most arrive Thursday.

To most of Europe. Costs appear at checkout once you enter an address.

Wholesale

Five kilos a week for trade prices. Below that you are welcome to buy at the normal price.

We lend grinders to wholesale customers and set them up on site.

title: Delivery and returns
content:
Delivery and returns

When it is roasted, and when it arrives

Coffee is posted the morning after it is roasted, so it reaches you within days of leaving the drum.

What it costs

Delivery

Standard delivery

$4.50, first class, two to three working days

Free delivery

On orders over $40, and on every subscription

Roast day

Tuesday. Order by Monday evening to be in that roast

Collection

Free from the arch on Saturday mornings

Europe

From $12, three to six working days

Returns

Coffee is food, so we cannot resell a bag once it has left us. If something is wrong with it -- and sometimes something is -- tell us within thirty days and we will replace it or refund it. You do not need to send it back.

Equipment

Send equipment back unused within thirty days for a full refund. Anything faulty is covered for two years; write to us and we will collect it.

Damaged in the post

Send a photograph of the box and the bag. We will have another in that week's roast, at no cost.
